finalExcerpt:
I fixed the bug, and all 5 tests pass (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`).

`parse_price` in `inventory.py` now treats commas as thousands separators when the whole string looks like `1,234.50` or `1,234,567`. That means groups of exactly three digits after the commas, followed by a dot or another comma group. Everything else still goes through the old decimal-comma path, so `"12,50"`, `"12.50"` and `"$3"` behave as before. `total_value` is unchanged.

A bare `"1,234"` (one comma group, no dot) is still read as a European decimal, giving `1.234`. The issue only calls a comma a thousands separator when a dot or another comma group follows, so I left that case alone.

I added a regression test, `test_thousands_separator`, in `tests/test_inventory.py`. It covers `"1,234.50"` → `1234.5` and `"$1,234,567"` → `1234567.0`.

I haven't committed anything.
